title: Growth1000 — agent workspace direction
question: Both directions follow your briefing-first, mobile-first specification. Choose the structure to build in code.

options.label: Client Dossier
options.thesis: One current brief, followed by decisions with their evidence attached.
options.viewport: Configured agent identity, a short briefing, and the most important decision; mobile navigation stays below.
options.risk: Needs careful copy editing so the case structure never becomes paperwork.

raised.raise: Declined: weaker business-owner identification and less room for actionable mobile copy.
Declined: technical framing weakens both audience fit and action clarity.
Declined: the metaphor makes business tasks harder to recognize and act on.
Declined: confrontational tone and styling distract from recommendations.
Declined: music-instrument controls reduce audience fit and task clarity.
Declined: gaming cues undermine professional trust and clarity.

options.label: Personal Briefing
options.thesis: A direct note from the agent leads into a short, prioritized action queue.
options.viewport: Business greeting and briefing first; one review action sits above supporting progress.
options.risk: Familiar and easy to use, but closer to other premium service portals.

options.label: Type specimen
options.thesis: An oversized finding headline with supporting evidence in compact text.
options.viewport: Large finding above two evidence blocks.
options.risk: Display pixels feel like a design experiment, not a trusted employee.
options.case: Declined: weaker business-owner identification and less room for actionable mobile copy.
options.kept: Keep unmistakable hierarchy without pixel styling.

options.label: Viewfinder
options.thesis: A business signal framed as the subject, with evidence at the edges.
options.viewport: One finding in a full-screen frame.
options.risk: Resembles a monitoring tool and disperses reading across corners.
options.case: Declined: technical framing weakens both audience fit and action clarity.
options.kept: Keep one unambiguous point of attention.

options.label: Garden
options.thesis: Opportunities grouped into connected areas of business growth.
options.viewport: One opportunity region with related next steps.
options.risk: Metaphorical navigation hides work and invites decorative motion.
options.case: Declined: the metaphor makes business tasks harder to recognize and act on.
options.kept: Keep relationships explicit without decorative simulation.

options.label: Industrial labels
options.thesis: Explicitly named work areas and highly visible decision states.
options.viewport: A plainly labelled briefing and approval cards.
options.risk: Hazard styling and shouting labels conflict with calm service.
options.case: Declined: confrontational tone and styling distract from recommendations.

options.label: Step sequence
options.thesis: The path from received request to completed work stays visible.
options.viewport: Request stages followed by today's decisions.
options.risk: A fixed unbroken step row fails the compact mobile requirement.
options.case: Declined: music-instrument controls reduce audience fit and task clarity.
options.kept: Keep clear sequence and immediate control feedback.

options.label: Arcade
options.thesis: Strong state distinctions organize tasks into discrete rooms.
options.viewport: A grid of work states and a highlighted next action.
options.risk: Glow and game metaphors violate the brief.
options.case: Declined: gaming cues undermine professional trust and clarity.
options.kept: Keep consistent state semantics without glow.

canonCard.label: Conventional service portal
canonCard.thesis: A familiar app shell with a briefing and action cards.
canonCard.viewport: A standard navigation shell with briefing before metrics.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand but less distinctive.
